Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Higher serum 25(OH)D levels were associated with lower depressive symptom severity (K-HDRS) in women with secondary amenorrhea, after adjusting for age and BMI.
Sentence: "The total score of the Korean version of the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (K-HDRS) was negatively related to serum 25(OH)D levels, free testosterone, and serum anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) after adjusting for age and BMI (r = −0.450, p < 0.001; r = −0.258, p = 0.045; and r = −0.339, p = 0.006, respectively)."
Measured as: depressive severity (K-HDRS total score)
Population: Korean women with secondary amenorrhea (63 analyzed of 78 recruited)
Intervention: Serum 25(OH)D level (observational exposure, no intervention)
Comparator: None; association across participants
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 78
baseline_vitamin_d_status: mixed

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: Mid-life serum 25(OH)D concentrations were not significantly associated with depressive symptoms 20 years later.
Sentence: "There was no significant association with functional ability or depressive symptoms."
Measured as: depressive symptoms
Population: 13,039 white and black ARIC participants, mean age 57 at mid-life, 57% women, 24% black
Intervention: Mid-life serum 25(OH)D concentration (observational exposure, visit 2)
Comparator: Higher vs lower 25(OH)D categories (deficient <20, intermediate 20-<30, sufficient >=30 ng/mL)
Design: cohort study
Sample size: 13,039
baseline_vitamin_d_status: mixed
